skill.name: container-grype
skill.description: Scan container images, filesystems, and SBOMs with Grype. Prioritize vulnerabilities using CVSS severity, EPSS probability, CISA KEV status, and CI/CD gate requirements.
skill.summary: Use Grype to scan containers and prioritize vulnerability remediation.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown examples, reference material, or CI variable syntax. Real risks remain in bundled CI templates: remote installer scripts are piped into shells, a Jenkins example mounts the Docker socket, one token is exposed to action code, and Tekton parameters are used unquoted in shell commands.

remediation.issue: Remote installer scripts are piped directly into bash or sh in CI examples.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell installs with pinned packages, verified release artifacts, or checksum validation before execution.

remediation.issue: The Jenkins example mounts the host Docker socket into the scanner container.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer registry or SBOM scans, rootless builders, remote Docker isolation, or a restricted socket proxy.

remediation.issue: Tekton scan commands interpolate parameters into shell commands without quoting or allowlist validation.
remediation.suggestion: Quote all parameter expansions and validate image references and severity thresholds before invoking Grype.

remediation.issue: CI examples use mutable scanner references and expose a GitHub token to action code.
remediation.suggestion: Pin actions and container images to immutable SHAs or digests, and set least-privilege workflow permissions.

content.value_statement: Container images often hide vulnerable packages and outdated dependencies. This skill guides Grype scans, CI gates, and remediation priorities.
actual_capabilities: Guides Grype scans for container images, local filesystems, and SBOM files.
Explains severity thresholds for CI/CD build gates using Grype fail policies.
Prioritizes findings with CVSS severity, EPSS probability, and CISA KEV status.
Provides example Grype configuration for ignores, exclusions, database cache, and output settings.
Maps scan outputs to reports for developers, security teams, and compliance workflows.
limitations: Requires Grype and container or SBOM access in the user environment.
Does not replace manual validation of exploitable vulnerabilities or compensating controls.
Scan accuracy depends on current vulnerability databases and package metadata.
Bundled CI examples need hardening before direct production use.

use_cases.title: Block Risky Container Releases
use_cases.description: Add Grype checks to CI pipelines and fail builds when critical or high vulnerabilities are present.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Remediation Work
use_cases.description: Review scan results with KEV, EPSS, and CVSS context to decide which fixes need immediate action.

use_cases.title: Audit SBOM Vulnerability Exposure
use_cases.description: Scan Syft, SPDX, or CycloneDX SBOMs and prepare evidence for vulnerability management reviews.

prompt_templates.title: Scan One Image
prompt_templates.prompt: Scan this container image with Grype and summarize critical and high vulnerabilities: <image-name>.

prompt_templates.title: Create a CI Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add a Grype CI gate that fails on high severity findings and uploads a readable report.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Grype scan results and rank remediation by KEV status, EPSS probability, CVSS score, and fix availability.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Enterprise Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Grype-based container vulnerability workflow for multiple registries, SBOM reuse, exceptions, reporting, and release gates.

output_examples.input: Scan a release image before deployment.
output: A concise risk summary by severity and affected package.
A release recommendation based on the configured fail threshold.
A remediation list ordered by exploited status and fix availability.

output_examples.input: Review Grype results from a CI run.
output: A build gate decision with the reason for pass or fail.
Top vulnerabilities with package names, versions, and suggested upgrade paths.
Notes for accepted risks that need documented expiration dates.

output_examples.input: Plan recurring SBOM scans for production services.
output: A workflow for SBOM generation, storage, rescanning, and reporting.
Suggested scan frequency and escalation criteria.
Controls for protecting scan artifacts and vulnerability reports.

best_practices: Update the Grype vulnerability database before important release scans.
Use strict fail thresholds for production images and document every exception.
Protect scan reports because package names and versions can reveal system design.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installer scripts directly into a shell in production CI.
Do not mount the Docker socket into scanner containers unless isolation risks are accepted.
Do not suppress vulnerabilities without a reason, owner, and review date.

faq.question: What does this skill scan?
faq.answer: It supports Grype scans for container images, directories, and SBOM files.

faq.question: Can it fail a CI build?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Grype fail thresholds so pipelines can block risky releases.

faq.question: Does it install Grype automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users must manage tool installation and trust decisions.

faq.question: How are vulnerabilities prioritized?
faq.answer: The workflow prioritizes CISA KEV entries, high EPSS probability, severe CVSS scores, and available fixes.

faq.question: Can it analyze SBOMs?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes scanning Syft, SPDX, and CycloneDX SBOMs with Grype.

faq.question: Is it ready for production CI?
faq.answer: The workflow is useful, but bundled CI examples need hardening before production use.
